endowed with the highest feminine virtues, seeing Prince

Accompanied for some leagues by King Dasaratha and his 
people, Rama dismissed the chariot on reaching the town of 
Shringavera on the banks of the Ganges, and commanded the 
minister Sumantta to return to the capital. 
Here the prince met his beloved Guha, the chief of the 
Cbandslas,• accompanied by whom, with Laksbmans and Sita,

forest like devas' or gandhsrvas.• 
Overwhelmed with grief at the separation from his sons and

was dwelling on the Chittrakuta mountain. 
The holy sages offered the throne, left vacant on the desth

Shri Bharata, touching the feet of Rama in submission.

brief.summary_1line: Narada tells Valmiki the life story of Rama—from virtues and exile to Sita’s abduction, Ravana’s defeat, and Rama’s just rule in Ayodhya.

image_candidates.scene_text: The sage Narada stands before Valmiki in a forest hermitage, describing the radiant blue‑hued prince Rama with celestial calm.
Hanuman leaps across the vast ocean toward the golden city of Lanka under a wide sky.
Sita steps calmly into a blazing fire before an assembly of gods and warriors to prove her purity.

deep.rich_summary: Sage Valmiki asks the divine sage Narada whether a perfect man exists—one who embodies virtue, courage, wisdom, truth, and compassion. Narada answers by recounting the life of Rama of the Ikshvaku line, describing his noble qualities and the great events of his life. He summarizes Rama’s exile due to Queen Kaikeyi’s demand, the loyal companionship of Sita and Lakshmana, and King Dasaratha’s death. In the forest Rama slays demons and later forms an alliance with the monkey king Sugriva after killing Bali. The search for Sita leads Hanuman to leap to Lanka, find her, and burn the city. Rama builds a bridge across the sea, defeats Ravana, proves Sita’s purity through the fire ordeal, and returns to rule Ayodhya in a just and prosperous reign—establishing the ideal of righteous kingship.

highlight_spans.why: Opening invocation introducing Valmiki and Narada and framing the quest for the ideal human being.
Narada’s declaration of Rama as the rare hero possessing the extraordinary virtues Valmiki seeks.
The pivotal moment when Ravana abducts Sita after the deceptive lure that draws Rama and Lakshmana away.
Hanuman’s leap across the ocean and discovery of Sita in Lanka—one of the epic’s most iconic mythic episodes.
Rama’s army crossing the ocean bridge and the climactic battle culminating in Ravana’s defeat.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana seizes Sita and lifts her into the sky in his chariot while the wounded vulture Jatayu falls below after trying to save her.
Hanuman launches across the vast ocean toward the golden city of Lanka, the wind whipping around him as the island fortress rises from the sea.
Rama’s vast monkey army storms Lanka as Rama confronts Ravana in a blazing battlefield of arrows, chariots, and shattered towers.
